---
title: "R for Bioinformatics"
subtitle: "From first principles to writing your own tools"
---

A hands-on course that takes you from basic R to building documented, tested, installable bioinformatics tools. Idiomatic, vector-first, tidyverse-forward — every example uses a pathogen-genomics theme.

## The five parts

| Part | Focus |
|---|---|
| [I — Foundations](PartI-theory.qmd) | the R mindset, vectors & strings, control flow, data structures, functions |
| [II — Real Programming](PartII-theory.qmd) | files (FASTA/FASTQ/CSV), errors/testing, S3/S4 objects |
| [III — Tidyverse](PartIII-theory.qmd) | apply/purrr, dplyr/tidyr, ggplot2, a full workflow |
| [IV — Bioconductor](PartIV-theory.qmd) | Biostrings, genomic ranges, real formats + a DE taste |
| [V — Reproducible](PartV-theory.qmd) | R Markdown/Quarto, writing an R package |

## Setup

```r
install.packages("tidyverse")
install.packages(c("testthat", "devtools", "roxygen2", "usethis", "rmarkdown"))
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("Biostrings", "GenomicRanges", "SummarizedExperiment"))
```

Download the example data from the repository's `data/` folder and keep it in your RStudio project.
